::: {.callout-note title="Before you start"}
Read [Your first composite model](diblock-copolymer.qmd) first. Use its
Python environment with `pyseb[visualization]` installed to run the gallery.
Run from `docs/tutorials` in a repository checkout so the catalogue helpers
and bundled model definitions are available.
:::

This page introduces what a subunit supplies and lets you explore the bundled
models. You do not need to define a new model to use those building blocks.

## What is a subunit?

A subunit is a reusable scattering component. It supplies its normalized form
factor, amplitudes relative to its reference points, phase factors between
those references, structural parameters, and size measures. pySEB connects
subunits through specific references such as a polymer end or sphere center,
or distributed references such as a contour or surface.

Subunits describe local scattering physics. A `World` supplies instance names,
parameter-sharing tags, links, and reusable nested structures. Keeping those
responsibilities separate lets one subunit definition participate in chains,
stars, micelles, dendrimers, and other composite models.

## Explore the bundled subunits

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

from _helpers import (
    bundled_subunit_catalogue,
    bundled_subunit_figure,
    bundled_subunit_markdown,
)

catalogue = bundled_subunit_catalogue()
print(bundled_subunit_markdown(catalogue))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-bundled-subunit-catalogue
#| fig-cap: "Bundled YAML subunits rendered automatically from their OpenUSD visualization definitions. Drag a panel to rotate it and scroll to zoom."
#| echo: false

catalogue_figure = bundled_subunit_figure(catalogue)
catalogue_figure.show(config={
    "displaylogo": False,
    "scrollZoom": True,
    "responsive": True,
})
```

The names and visual gallery are generated from `models/*.pyseb.yaml` during
the documentation build. A newly bundled model appears automatically when it
provides visualization metadata and a validation case containing values for
all structural parameters. The
[Subunit Catalogue](https://github.com/Tobionecenobi/pySEB/wiki/Subunit-Catalogue)
remains the reference for equations, parameters, and reference points.

The model/unfolded button switches the entire gallery. Isolated rigid subunits
look the same in both layouts: they have no internal joint to unfold.

## Choose a model

Choose a bundled model and identify its parameters and link references in the
[Subunit Catalogue](https://github.com/Tobionecenobi/pySEB/wiki/Subunit-Catalogue).
For example, a rod has endpoint references, while a sphere also has a
distributed surface reference. Which would you use for a rigid spacer?

## Continue

[Symbolic expressions and export](symbolic-expressions.qmd) shows how to print
the equations of a model and export them for use elsewhere.

To derive your own equations step by step, start with
[Contribute your own subunit](contribute-subunit.qmd). The five-page sequence
introduces F, A, Ψ, distributed references, visualization, and validation using
one spherical shell. For a shorter registration example, see
[Define and validate a custom subunit](define-custom-subunit.qmd).
For distributed surface links, try the [micelle tutorial](micelle.qmd).
